clue.text: Start of play, but not in 11

definitions.text: Start of play, but not in 11

parts.words: Start of play, but not in 11
parts.note: the opening performance of a stage play, which is not how a cricket match (the answer at 11) begins: there the start is the first innings or first day

explanation.surface: A remark that play has begun, though not in some other game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a game, as 11 (CRICKET MATCH) suggests, but it is the theatre: a premiere, a term a match never uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical premiere is the opening performance, the start of a play's run.

clue.text: Children's stories

parts.note: not books for the young but the small untruths children tell, also called stories

explanation.definitionFit: Small lies are often called stories, especially when children tell them.

clue.text: Pigeons disliked by bad sailors

definitions.meaning: a breed of tumbling pigeon that turns over in flight
long heavy swell waves that make poor sailors seasick

explanation.definitionFit: Tumbler pigeons are one sense; long heavy ocean waves, which upset weak stomachs, are the other.

clue.text: Complete contents of 9 in a way

parts.note: thorough means complete or utter
what a bill of fare (9 across) lists is food, or fare

explanation.surface: An entire list of dishes arranged in some fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street is a way through.

clue.text: Degrading to delve down under ?

parts.note: infra is Latin for below or underneath
to dig is to delve

explanation.surface: Humiliating to have to dig in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' suggests Australia but means the Latin INFRA, below; INFRA DIG is short for infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for a Latin phrase meaning beneath one's dignity, so demeaning.

clue.text: For this object look into the retort

indicators.note: look into tells us to search inside the words the retort for the answer

explanation.surface: Advice to peer into a laboratory vessel for a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: An old formal word meaning to this or for this purpose.

clue.text: Something to put on and brag about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of brag are turned around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A garment that is worn and boasted of.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, which is what one puts on.

clue.text: Easing nothing in the form of torture

indicators.note: in the form of says the letters are reshaped into a new word

parts.note: O, the round figure nought, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Relief that is no relief, only a kind of torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in agony over something is to be tormented by it.

clue.text: One whose cares are very little ones

definitions.text: One whose cares are very little ones

parts.words: One whose cares are very little ones
parts.note: a person minding infants: the cares are not trivial worries but the tiny children in their charge

explanation.definitionFit: A person minding infants while parents are out has the very young in their care.

clue.text: It shows choice of food, rather than its cost

definitions.text: It shows choice of food, rather than its cost

parts.words: It shows choice of food, rather than its cost
parts.note: a bill usually states a cost, but this kind of bill lists the dishes on offer instead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests the reckoning at the end of a meal; the clue turns this round to the list of dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for a restaurant menu, the list of dishes from which diners choose.

clue.text: It makes a cox look foppish

definitions.text: It makes a cox look foppish

parts.words: It makes a cox look foppish
parts.note: attach this word to cox and you get ..., an old word for a vain dandy or fop

explanation.walkthrough: A cox steers a rowing boat; the clue is really about spelling, since cox plus this word gives COXCOMB, a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain dandy, so the toothed grooming tool turns a cox into one.

clue.text: This is played' over and over again

definitions.text: This is played' over and over again

parts.words: This is played' over and over again
parts.note: in cricket the game is made of overs, sets of six balls, bowled one after another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over and over again' sounds like a repeated song; in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket game consists of many overs, each of six balls.

clue.text: The hour for battle is not on the clock

definitions.text: The hour for battle is not on the clock

parts.words: The hour for battle is not on the clock
parts.note: military ... hour is when an attack begins, yet no clock face shows a nought

explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the time set for an attack, and nought is the number missing from a clock face.

clue.text: Unearthly result of radio sets being out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of radio sets are jumbled into a different sequence

explanation.surface: Broken wireless receivers produce strange, otherworldly noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor planets are bodies beyond our world, hence unearthly.

clue.text: If made redundant they would naturally be' dispirited

definitions.text: If made redundant they would naturally be' dispirited

parts.words: If made redundant they would naturally be' dispirited
parts.note: workers who make whisky and gin would, if sacked, be without spirits in both senses

explanation.definitionFit: Makers of whisky and gin produce spirits, so losing the job leaves them dispirited.

clue.text: Wear for the office

parts.note: not workday clothes but the badges and emblems that mark a position of authority

explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' suggests a workplace and its dress code; it means an official post, whose emblems are worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges or emblems of rank are worn to show one's official position.

clue.text: Stress can be acute

definitions.meaning: emphasis laid on a syllable in speech
an acute is one kind of diacritic mark, alongside grave and circumflex

explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis on a syllable is one meaning; a mark over a letter such as the acute is the other.

clue.text: Old wagon tax goes to the wall

parts.note: wain is an archaic word for a farm wagon
scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: An antique cart's levy is a lost cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panelling fitted to the lower part of a room's wall.

clue.text: Economy in plant

definitions.meaning: the sea pink, a coastal flowering plant

explanation.definitionFit: Frugality is one sense; the other is the sea pink, a coastal flower with the same name.

clue.text: Regret including even this in your tax return ?

indicators.note: including means one word is held inside the other

parts.note: to rue is to regret
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lamenting the income one declares to the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: Income or earnings, the money declared to the tax authorities.

clue.text: Many a football arbiter misses a point, being light hearted

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: misses means a letter is left out of the official's title

parts.note: the official who rules on a football match is the referee
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A football referee who fails to award a point remains cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of worries means cheerful, untroubled and buoyant.

clue.text: In need of an invigorating wind, perhaps

definitions.text: In need of an invigorating wind, perhaps

parts.words: In need of an invigorating wind, perhaps
parts.note: a tired person needs a tonic, and a clock that has stopped needs winding up

explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and exhausted, like a clock whose spring has unwound.

clue.text: She claims to be an essayist

parts.note: am, as in a claim of I am
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A woman asserts that she writes essays.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, fitting a clue that refers to a female person.

clue.text: City personages of irritable disposition ?

parts.note: members of the City of London livery companies, read playfully as men who are liverish, that is irritable

explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's ancient trade guilds are livery companies; 'liverish' means bad-tempered, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a City guild wear its livery; liverish suggests a bad temper.

clue.text: People with universal 9

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 9 across, a list of dishes

parts.note: men is a word for people
U is the British film rating meaning universal, suitable for all

explanation.definitionFit: A list of dishes is the same thing as a bill of fare.

clue.text: One bent on submission

parts.note: not a person determined to yield but a joint that bends when someone ... in submission

explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint bends when one kneels in homage or surrender.

clue.text: She goes east and comes back

indicators.note: comes back tells us the word and is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: A woman travels east and then returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so a fair answer to a clue for a female person.

clue.text: Walking-stick for winter .

parts.note: a cane cut from the sloe bush, which also names the cold spell when that shrub flowers in early spring

explanation.walkthrough: A 'blackthorn winter' is a cold snap in spring when the sloe blossoms; sticks of its wood are traditional canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloe wood makes a classic cane, and a spring cold spell takes the shrub's name.

clue.text: Escorts both ways'

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads identically from left to right and from right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A note that someone accompanies another in each direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone home or to the door is to accompany them.

clue.text: Snob's opportunity to give an ultimatum ?'

definitions.text: Snob's opportunity to give an ultimatum ?

parts.words: Snob's opportunity to give an ultimatum ?
parts.note: snob is old slang for a shoemaker, whose tool is a last, so his opportunity is a ..., the phrase used in a final warning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snob' once meant a cobbler; a cobbler's last is the foot-shaped block he works on.
explanation.definitionFit: A final opportunity is what an ultimatum offers before consequences follow.
